title: Introduce aggregation-windows and contextual alert annotator
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds multi-scale aggregation windows for token cost and latency metrics and a contextual alert annotator that enriches alerts with pre-computed window summaries and correlated log snippets. Reduces noisy long-tail alerting and accelerates incident triage.
description:
Motivation: We see frequent noisy alerts for token-cost and per-invocation latency spikes driven by short-lived bursts or downstream noise. Root cause triage requires manually assembling time-windowed context (short/medium/long) and correlating logs and kv-cache metrics. This PR introduces two pieces: 1) aggregation_windows: a lightweight pipeline that generates 3 rolling summaries (30s, 5m, 30m) for key token-level metrics (tokens_inflight, token_cost, generation_latency, kv_cache_hit_rate) and stores them as compact time-series rollups. 2) contextual_alert_annotator: an enrichment service that attaches the latest aggregation window snapshot plus the top-3 correlated log snippets and top-2 trace span IDs to alerts at creation time.

What changed (summary of commits): commit 1: telemetry: add aggregation_windows service and scheduler (src/telemetry/aggregation_windows.py, tests/test_aggregation_windows.py) commit 2: storage: compact rollup proto and migration (migrations/20260218_rollup_proto.sql, src/storage/rollup_writer.py) commit 3: alerts: introduce annotator and hook into alert dispatch pipeline (src/alerts/annotator.py, src/alerts/hooks.py) commit 4: dashboards: new aggregation-windows overview panel and templated alert-preview widget (dashboards/aggregation_windows_overview.json) commit 5: docs and runbooks (docs/obs/aggregation-windows.md, runbooks/annotator-troubleshoot.md) commit 6: tests and e2e harness updates (tests/e2e/alert_annotator_e2e.py)

Files touched (high-level): src/telemetry/aggregation_windows.py, src/storage/rollup_writer.py, src/alerts/annotator.py, src/alerts/hooks.py, dashboards/aggregation_windows_overview.json, docs/obs/aggregation-windows.md, runbooks/annotator-troubleshoot.md, migrations/20260218_rollup_proto.sql, tests/test_aggregation_windows.py, tests/e2e/alert_annotator_e2e.py

Design notes: - Aggregation windows are computed using the existing streaming metrics pipeline with a new compact rollup proto to keep storage footprint small (approx 6 bytes per metric per window). We intentionally limit the set of metrics to token-centric signals to avoid cardinality explosion. - The annotator runs synchronously during alert creation but fetches the most recent rollup snapshot (cached) to avoid extra tail latency. For heavy alerts we attach only metadata pointers; full rollup fetch remains asynchronous. - Correlation uses existing log-index service with an adjustable score (configurable threshold) and returns a sanitized snippet. Access control respects tenant isolation; no raw logs are embedded in alert payloads for hosted customers.

Checklist: - [x] Aggregation window computation and writer - [x] Rollup proto and migration - [x] Annotator integration with alert pipeline - [x] Dashboard and alert-preview widget - [x] Unit tests and e2e sim - [x] Runbook and docs

Review conversation (high-level): Connor Liu: "Nice approach — can we keep the 30m window optional per-tenant to control storage?" Author (Aisha): "Yes, added per-tenant window toggles in config with sensible defaults; see src/telemetry/config.py." Diego Ramos: "Annotator could cause noise if log correlation returns irrelevant snippets; add a relevance threshold." Author: "Added a configurable scoring threshold and a fallback to omit snippets if score < 0.35." Priya Nair: "Migration looks safe but add a backfill plan." Author: "Included a lightweight backfill tool (scripts/backfill_rollups.py) and a runbook step; backfill is optional and idempotent."

CI notes: Initial CI run showed a flaky e2e related to synthetic traces timing; reran the e2e job and it passed. All unit tests pass; linter fixed. Performance tests: small regression (~1.6% tail latency in alert creation path when annotator runs synchronous fetch) observed in perf job but within SLO; added cache TTL and async pointer-fallback to mitigate.

Merging: After approvals from reviewers and sign-off on migration/backfill plan, PR was squash-merged on 2026-02-24 using "squash and merge". Merge commit includes summary and links to runbook.

How to validate after deploy: - Use dashboards/aggregation_windows_overview.json to inspect windowed summaries. - Trigger synthetic alert via tests/e2e/alert_annotator_e2e.py to verify annotated payload includes rollup_snapshot pointer and optionally inline log snippets when relevance score is high. - Run the backfill script in a staging environment for tenants that opted in.

Follow-ups: - ENG-4330: add per-route windowing to capture cold-starts in rarely used models. - ENG-4219: surface rollup-derived anomaly scores to the alerting engine for adaptive thresholds.

Notes for on-call: Annotator failures are non-fatal; alerts still fire without enrichment. In case of storage write issues, rollups will back off and alerting will trigger an internal SRE signal (internal/ops) — see runbooks/annotator-troubleshoot.md for recovery steps.
